title.narrative: Safeguarding Lives and Dignity through Integrated Nutrition and WASH Response in Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian crisis in northeast Nigeria continues to generate severe needs, particularly in Borno State, where protracted conflict, displacement, and recurrent flooding have eroded community resilience. In Kaga and Konduga LGAs, unsafe water, poor hygiene, and widespread malnutrition continue to endanger the health and dignity of affected populations. This six-month intervention seeks to safeguard lives and restore dignity through an integrated, life-saving Nutrition and WASH response, with protection, gender, and disability inclusion mainstreamed across all components. The project will directly reach 20,900 individuals—comprising 9,000 IDPs and 11,900 host community members across Kaga and Konduga LGAs..lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUnder the Nutrition component, the project will enhance early detection and treatment of acute malnutrition among children aged 6–59 months through community-based screening and referral systems. A total of 6,000 children will be screened using MUAC, with approximately 1,500 MAM cases enrolled in Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs (TSFP) following CMAM guidelines. To promote sustained behavior change, five cooking demonstration sessions will showcase preparation of balanced, affordable meals using locally available foods. These efforts directly contribute to Nutrition Cluster objectives of improving access to curative and preventive nutrition services (SS01 and SS02).ltbrgtThe WASH component addresses the acute shortage of safe water and inadequate hygiene conditions in both LGAs. The project will rehabilitate and solarize 6 non-functional water points, restoring safe water access for at least 9,000 people. Rehabilitated facilities will incorporate ramps, lighting, and drainage systems to ensure safety, privacy, and accessibility for women, children, and persons with disabilities. To sustain impact, six WASH committees (with at least 30% female membership) will be trained in water system operation, maintenance, and quality monitoring. In parallel, 1,160 WASH NFI kits—including buckets, jerry cans, soap, and purification tablets—will be distributed to vulnerable households, while hygiene promotion campaigns will reach 9,000 individuals with key messages on handwashing, menstrual hygiene management, safe water handling, and cholera prevention.ltbrgtProtection is mainstreamed throughout the project to ensure that all interventions uphold safety, dignity, and inclusion. Under Nutrition, caregivers will receive sensitization on safeguarding and PSEA, while WASH infrastructure will be designed to reduce exposure to GBV risks. Community volunteers, WASH committees, and staff will be trained on inclusion, safeguarding, and accountability to affected populations, guided by the “do no harm” principle.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
